_comment: Dialogue (issue #11, scripts/dialogue.gd). A line is [speaker, text] or [speaker, text, expression]. speaker: a recruit id, a key of speakers (people who are not recruits) or "" for narration. expression picks assets/portraits/<id>_<expression>.png (happy, angry, sad, surprised, smug), falling back to <id>.png, then to a drawn placeholder. talks: conversations played in the dialogue box (VN style); each plays once per campaign where the game says so. first_talk: recruit id -> the talk that plays the first time Ash speaks to them in Hollowmark (after that they say their usual lines). events: banter for things that happen (once: true = once per campaign; urgent: true = jumps the queue); every speaker must be present. banter: walking banter zones per map (the map file's name). rect is [x, y, width, height] in 16px tiles; walking into it plays the lines once per campaign, at the top of the screen, without stopping the game. needs: extra ids that must be present. On missions 'present' is the living party; in Hollowmark it is whoever is standing in town.

meadow_intro.title: The Frayed Meadow
lines: Grass. Wind. A sky with all its edges still on. Behind you, the white hush of the Blank, sulking that it let you go.
Huh. A person. Or a very convincing smudge.
You crawled out of that? Nobody crawls out of that. Nobody's paid me to see it, neither.
He looks you over the way a fence looks over a stolen candlestick.
No name? No? Fine. You look like somethin' left over after a fire. Ash, then. Don't thank me, it's on the bill.
Them white things are Nibblers. They eat. 'It 'em when your gauge is full, or don't, and I'll invoice your corpse.
Hollowmark's east of 'ere. What's left of it. Stay close and try not to get erased before payday.

quill_first.title: The Quartermaster
lines: Ah. The thing that walked out of the Blank. Hold still, I need to file you.
Quill flips through a ledger as thick as a doorstep, licks a thumb, flips again.
Name: none. Debts: none. Taxable property: one cloak, scorched, herewith noted. You are the cleanest account I have ever seen.
I kept these books for the Concord eleven years. Every coin in, every coin out, every family struck through for non-payment.
Now the Concord's gone quiet and the Blank is eating the margins. So I keep them for whoever keeps the lights on.
Which, apparently, is you. Don't look so worried. I'm very good at making numbers behave.

tobble_first.title: The Spilt Ink
lines: Sit, sit. You're the quiet one everyone's whispering about. Whispering's my trade, so you're good for business.
He pours something the colour of old varnish and slides it over without asking.
Thirty year I've been about to retire. Then the Blank took the road south, and the road north, and my pension with 'em.
So I stay. I pour. People talk after the third cup, and I remember it after the fourth.
You want to know who's lying in this town, you come to me. First secret's free. After that we haggle.

pell_first.title: The Gravedigger
lines: Mind the hole. And that one. And, well. Mind all of 'em, proper.
Fresh graves in a neat row, each one empty, each one exactly the right size for someone.
I dig 'em in the morning. By the evening, someone fits. Don't ask me how I know the sizes. I don't, ar.
Funny thing about the Blank, though. Doesn't leave bodies. My graves are filling up slower every week, I reckon.
Measured you while you were walking over, by the way. Proper lovely shape for it, you are. No offence.

gristle_first.title: The Hedge-Witch
lines: So you're the one who dragged me out of that bog. I'd thank you, but gratitude's bad for the complexion.
She's sorting bottles by smell. Two of them smoke when she uncorks them.
This one cures fever. This one gives it. Same recipe, different dose. Most things in life are like that, isn't it.
I'll patch your people up. I'll bill them for it too, itemised, with interest. Ask the mercenary, seen my rates, he has.
And if your Blank ever gets a fever, dearie, you send it to me.

ninefingers_first.title: The Deserter
lines: Before you ask: yes, nine. Yes, it's the paperwork's fault. No, I won't draw you a diagram.
Concord gave me an order to strike out a village. Pen, not sword. Cleaner, they said. No bodies, no screaming.
Tore up the order. They took the finger I signed things with. Seemed fair at the time.
They flex the hand. The gap is old and neat.
So. Collecting strays who said no to someone. Can work with that.

abeyance_first.title: The Runaway Scribe
lines: Oh. It's you. The page said you'd come over about now. It also said you'd be taller, so it isn't always right.
She holds up a single sheet of vellum. The ink on it crawls, slowly, like ants rearranging a sentence.
I stole it from the Abbey. It rewrites itself every night. Last night it wrote a name. Yours. You don't have one.
The ink-sickness makes me hear things. Mostly polite things. Mostly.
I'd like to stay near you, if that's permitted. Whatever's writing on this page seems very interested in where you go.

auditor_intro.title: The Tithe Road Tollgate
lines: The tollgate is too quiet. Someone has swept the road. Someone has swept the birds off it, too.
A tall figure in black stands at the gate, writing. Its quill is longer than a pike, and it does not drip. It would not dare.
I am the Auditor, Concord Office of Corrections. I have reviewed Hollowmark. Its taxes are unpaid, its governor has absconded, and it is currently being run by a person who does not exist.
It has been noted that you are not on the Ledger. Your town will duly join you.
He turns a page. Somewhere behind you, a fence post quietly stops having been there.
Hold still. This will not hurt. Nothing that never happened can hurt.

auditor_phase2.title: Final Notice
lines: Irregular. Highly irregular. You should have been struck out three times by now.
He signs the air. Ink runs down the quill like it has somewhere urgent to be. Clerks crawl out of the margins to help.

auditor_outro.title: Struck Out
lines: The great quill splits down the shaft with a sound like a ledger slammed shut.
This... is not... in the procedures.
You cannot strike out a Corrections officer. There is no form for it. There is no form for YOU.
His edges go first, then his title, then his name. The last thing to fade is a neat signature, still waiting for a date.
The tollgate creaks open. The road to Hollowmark is yours, and so, apparently, is the paperwork.

ottoline_first.title: The Doorframe
lines: Big Ottoline has to duck to look at Ash, and she does it slowly, like a drawbridge coming down.
Our Tobble says you're all right. Our Tobble also says his knees can tell the weather. So I'll make my own mind up.
Kept doors my whole life. Taverns. A cabaret. A magistrate's office, briefly, from the outside.
Here's how it goes. I stand in front. Owt that wants you comes through me first. They usually think again.
Don't thank me. Just don't wander off where I can't see you.

jessamy_first.title: Night Shift
lines: There you are. Been watchin' you all day from the shady side of the plaza. Don't be flattered. Be a little flattered.
Guild terms: I move whatever you need moved, after dark, and you don't ask what's in the crates.
She tilts her face out of a patch of sunlight, quickly, the way you'd pull your hand back from a stove.
And I don't do mornings. Or noons. Or afternoons, really. Send for me once the lamps are lit, handsome. Or pretty. Whichever.

odile_first.title: Audit Notice
lines: I have reviewed Hollowmark's books. All of them. Including the set under the floor of the stores.
Quill's beautiful books are a work of art. Quill's true books are a work of fiction with numbers in.
I brought the Concord's ledger with me. Every village they meant to collect, and the price they put on each. They want it back rather badly.
I should prefer they paid for it. So. Where do I sit?

velvette_first.title: Opening Night
lines: There you are. The one the Blank spat out. I expected you taller. I always expect people taller.
I don't fight for coin, darling. I fight for an audience. And right now the whole Inklands, it is watching you.
She draws the rapier an inch, just to hear it sing, and slides it home.
You may have my sword arm. My back, if you earn it. My secrets cost extra. Everyone pays eventually.

hortense_first.title: A Guest
lines: So this is Hollowmark. You did warn me about the mud. You did not warn me about the charm. I mean the town's, sweet, though also yours.
I shall need a room, a mirror and a reason to stay. The first two I can find myself.
She looks round the square once, the way a duellist looks round a hall: every door, every window, who is watching.
Lovely. Nobody here is trying to kill me. I may have to start a rumour, or I shall be bored by Thursday.

saffron_first.title: Opening Act
lines: Right, love. Where do I sing? Every town's got a spot. A step, a cart, a dead tree. Somewhere folk stop.
The well. Perfect. Good echo, terrible water. Like most of my old dressing rooms.
She hums two bars at the well, and for a breath there is a bucket on the rope that nobody put there. Then there isn't.
Don't mind that. Happens when I'm settling in. I'll keep it to sparrows and lamps till everyone's used to me.

nan_first.title: Terms and Conditions
lines: Nan Cripps, on the payroll! I'll need a stall, a stool and somebody who doesn't count their change. Is Quill spoken for?
Quill counts everything twice. Leave him alone.
That's Tally. My shadow. He talks, he's honest and he's not paid. Don't let him tell you different.
I am not paid. She is right about that one.
It popped. Like a thought you weren't supposed to have.
Ten. I'm charging by the 'ead, by the way. You owe me... a number.
Swinging at half power? Bold. Wait for the gauge, smudge.
Back in the grass. Try to come home with the same number of limbs.
That's the lot. Hollowmark's this way. Probably. Roads keep forgettin' themselves.
Population two 'undred and twelve. Then forty. Then a question mark. Somebody's been keeping score.
Don't look at me. Can't read. I can count, though, and that sign's goin' the wrong way.
Stump circle. Locals left offerings 'ere. Bread, buttons, the odd tooth.
"Please do not feed the silence." Bit late for that.
Don't drink that. Things look back out of it these days.
In the water, your reflection is a beat behind you. Then it catches up.
Bones. Good. Bones mean somethin' died here the honest way.
The Blank don't leave any. You just stop being on the list.
"Hollowmark, east." And under it: "east is gone." Someone 'ad a sense of humour about it.
Town's still there. Mostly. Road to it ain't. We'll go the long way.
'Ear that? It's humming. The Blank hums when it's hungry.
Step back. It spat you out once. It won't make the same mistake twice.
Ever fought something with no face, Ottoline?
Every Saturday night at the Encore. Drunks. Same thing.
Ottoline, chérie. Remember when you used to keep my door?
I remember you climbing out the window so you'd not pay the band.
Six weeks' wages is not an artistic difference.
You walk past my door again without coming in, I'll start a rumour about thee. A good one. Worse.
Careful! That one's not ready yet. Well. It's ready. Nobody's ready for it.
If you're thinking of borrowing from the stores, kindly write it down first. I'll know either way.
Gate's quiet. I 'ate quiet. Quiet means nobody's paying nobody to be loud.
Ottoline, love, stop glaring at the customers.
I'm not glaring. This is my face. Been my face since I were four.
She glared at the midwife. True story. Midwife apologised.
Jessamy, chérie, you are doing that thing where you stand in the shade as if it owes you money.
It does. Shade's very reliable. Unlike certain performers.
Name me. Go on. I adore it.
Quill. Your stores count says eleven days of turnips.
The other two are in the beautiful books.
I'm stood in everyone's light, Tolley. It's a public service.
You're looking peaky, dearie. Translucent, almost. There's a face on you.
It's the Ledger. Smell a struck-out line from here, I can. Come by the shop. First visit's free. The second one'll cost you your shadow.
Funny. People usually want the other thing.
Fog on the reeds, reeds in the fog. Darling, it is like a dressing room nobody has cleaned since the war.
I ran crates through here two years. There's a smugglers' path under the water, if you know where to step.
Penhallow. Know that name. Assessors' office, Old Mill.
My mother's office. I was the one who checked her sums.
Then you know what they do here.
I know what it costs. Down to the copper. That is worse.
Ottoline, you have walked into four low branches.
This one did. After I hit it back.
Toll post ahead. Smile, Odile. The pennies'll think we're honest.
That's what makes it such a good disguise.
Brannoc, darling, your contract arm is twitching.
Does that near Concord ink. Smells the paperwork.
How romantic. Mine only twitches near men who owe me money.
